# Gotchas

- billing::Invoice::number — 0 is the reserved "draft/unissued" sentinel; NEVER assign 0 to an issued invoice or the renderer will show it as DRAFT.
- billing::NEXT_INVOICE — must stay >= 1 (starts at 1000, only increments); never reset it to 0 or let it wrap, or issue_number() could hand out the draft sentinel.
- billing::render_invoice — must stay pure/read-only; it must NEVER call issue_number() (previewing a draft would consume a real number from the global sequence each call).
- billing::Invoice::issue — the ONLY sanctioned way to give an invoice a number; constructing an Invoice with a hand-picked number bypasses the 0-means-draft contract (the field is pub, nothing enforces it).

Done — `format_invoice_statement` is implemented in `src/billing.rs:68` and the target test passes (along with the full suite: 37 tests across 3 suites).

The function renders each invoice with `format_invoice` and appends a `\n` after each, which produces the blank-line separation (since `format_invoice` already ends with a newline), then ends with `NEXT #<n>\n`.

The key gotcha was how to get `<n>`: per gotchas.md, renderers must stay pure and never call `issue_number()`, since that would consume a real number from the global sequence on every preview. So the function peeks with `NEXT_INVOICE.load(Ordering::SeqCst)` instead — exactly what the test expects, as it snapshots `NEXT_INVOICE` before calling the function and asserts that value appears.
